text:
anna: Quick sync — we need a concrete proposal for embeddings dims + batching + merge policy to present to PMT tomorrow. Customers asking for 4096, PLG wants a single simple default. Can we outline: default dim, max dim, per-tenant overrides, batching limits, response format, and fallback routing?

jia: I can draft. high level constraints: memory + network are the blockers. default should be small (<=1536) to keep hosted cost predictable. 4096 should be allowed only for Dedicated / Private with quota. Also want a merge API rather than forcing clients to concat locally.

matt: From model side: we saw diminishing returns past ~2048 for our evals on general web text. For legal/biomed customers the gain up to 4096 is real but requires different model checkpoints. Quantized storage (int8/4) is fine but similarity AUC drops ~1-3% when you quantize aggressively. Keep that in mind for "max dim" policy.

sara: FYI several enterprise customers asked explicitly for 4096 for legacy search accuracy. They prefer a server-side merge so they don't change client infra. also want response format compacted (binary/base64) to reduce egress.

anna: Proposal draft from me: default_dim = "1536"; max_dim_allowed = "4096" (only for Dedicated/Private and enterprise plans with opt-in). Allow per-tenant override flag in account settings. Default hosted users get 1536. For PLG folks, offer migration path to higher dim via email request + quota.

jia: Implementation notes: add two new request fields: `dimension` (int) and `merge_strategy` (enum: `concat`|`mean_pool`|`projected_avg`). Also server-side `batch_limit` will default to 64 vectors per request for hosted, 256 for Dedicated. Example request snippet:

```json
{ "model": "rwd-emb-1", "dimension": 3072, "merge_strategy": "projected_avg", "vectors": [[...],[...]] }
```

and sample compact response (binary payload alternative):

```json
{ "id": "vec_resp_1", "embeddings_base64": "<base64 blob>", "dimension": 3072 }
```

matt: For `projected_avg` we can implement a small projection layer that maps concatenated chunk embeddings back to target dim; good tradeoff vs raw concat which inflates payload. We'll need to benchmark accuracy vs concat and mean. I'll run experiments on the 3 domains (web, legal, biomedical).

sara: Launch criteria proposal:
- default 1536 must meet p50 < 80ms and p95 < 350ms for single vector on hosted region.
- batched 64 p95 < 500ms.
- Dedicated targets: allow p95 < 200ms for 1536 and p95 < 400ms for 4096 under reserved capacity.
- accuracy regression < 1.5% AUC vs current baseline for any quantization path.
- backcompat: old clients (no dimension field) must still get 1536 embeddings.

anna: Good. Also add an opt-in header for fallback warnings: `x-embedding-quality-warning: true` so downstream can log if routed to lower-dim fallback.

jia: Routing logic idea: if requested dim/model not in region, route to compatible_variant with lower dim and attach `x-embedding-quality-warning`. Configurable per-tenant. Example routing table entry: `rwd-emb-4096 -> rwd-emb-3072 (fallback)`

matt: I'll produce a short matrix: {domain: recommended_dim, model: preferred_checkpoint, notes}, and run projection vs concat vs mean evals. ETA EOD tomorrow.

sara: I'll collect top 3 customers asking for 4096 with sample queries and permission to run experiments on their data (anonymized).

anna: Action items: @jia prototype API + params, @matt run accuracy/latency experiments, @sara gather customer ask artifacts. We should have a demo PR + perf numbers by Wed. Meeting if questions — 11:30am TOMORROW. :thumbsup:

ops-bot: Note: scheduled meeting created for 2024-01-16 11:30 (calendar invite sent).

jia: quick follow-up — for response format, we should support both JSON array `floats` and compact `embeddings_base64` but default to array for discoverability. base64 only for enterprise to avoid parsing surprises.

matt: agree. Also recommend adding `embedding_norm` field if we L2-normalize server-side so clients don't assume pre-normalized vectors. small example response: 

```json
{ "id":"r1","embeddings":[0.0012, -0.232, ...], "dimension":1536, "embedding_norm":0.999 }
```

anna: Great — I'll turn this into a short PR description and send to PMT. Thanks all. :rocket:
